stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that was promised a certificate
The group that drew without a reward

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They hypothesized that the number of other people present would affect the reporting of an emergency.

**Participants.** The sample was 80 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

**Results.** The group that waited with four other people: mean time before reporting (s) = 196. The group that waited alone: mean time before reporting (s) = 58. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the microsystem?

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace
options.why: That describes the exosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child
options.why: That describes the chronosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school
options.why: Correct. This is what the microsystem means.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child
options.why: That describes the macrosystem.

questions.explanation: The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.

questions.stem: Eight people with social anxiety meet weekly with one therapist, share their experiences and practice skills together. Which kind of therapy is this?

options.why: Dream interpretation is the psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts.
Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Correct. Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.

questions.explanation: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes confirmation bias?

options.text: The tendency to favor the members of one's own group
options.why: That describes in-group bias.

options.text: The tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike
options.why: That describes out-group homogeneity bias.

options.text: The tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited
options.why: That describes belief perseverance.

options.text: The tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes
options.why: Correct. This is what confirmation bias means.

questions.explanation: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Flat affect, loss of motivation and social withdrawal involve the absence of normal behaviors. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
Correct. A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.explanation: A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Workers do extra shifts to earn money, which they can exchange for things they want. Money is which kind of reinforcer?

options.why: Learned helplessness is the passive giving up that follows repeated experiences of being unable to avoid bad events.
Shaping is the reinforcing of closer and closer approximations of a desired behavior.
Instinctive drift is the tendency of a trained animal to return to its natural, inborn behaviors.
Correct. A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.explanation: A secondary reinforcer is a reinforcer, such as money or praise, that gets its power through association with other rewards.

questions.stem: As a friend walks away, her image on Tom's retina shrinks, but he does not think she is getting smaller. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Correct. Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Inside the spinal cord, some cells link the incoming pain message to the outgoing movement message. Which cells are these?

options.why: Correct. Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.explanation: Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.stem: A researcher sits quietly in a playground and records how often children share toys. Which research method is this?

options.why: Falsifiability is the quality of a claim that it could be shown to be wrong by evidence.
A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
Correct. Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.explanation: Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return?

options.why: Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.
Correct. Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.
Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.
Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.

questions.explanation: Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.stem: Students are 90 percent sure of answers that turn out to be right only 60 percent of the time. Which tendency is this?

options.why: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Correct. Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.explanation: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.stem: When a toy is hidden under a blanket, a five-month-old acts as if it has vanished, but a ten-month-old lifts the blanket to find it. What has the older infant developed?

options.why: Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Correct. Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.

questions.explanation: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: The gratitude group reported higher life satisfaction. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The type of journal caused the difference in subjective well-being
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The type of journal and subjective well-being are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes insight learning?

options.text: The sudden realization of the solution to a problem
options.why: Correct. This is what insight learning means.

options.text: The process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate
options.why: That describes modeling.

options.text: A mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings
options.why: That describes a cognitive map.

options.text: Learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior
options.why: That describes vicarious conditioning.

questions.explanation: Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.

questions.stem: Kwame repeats a phone number under his breath to keep it in mind. Which part of working memory is he using?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Correct. The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory?

options.why: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
The forgetting curve is the pattern in which memory fades quickly at first and then levels off.
Correct. Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.stem: Mr. Diaz snores loudly, stops breathing many times each night, and feels exhausted during the day. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Correct. Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.explanation: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness?

options.why: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.stem: The word 'unkindly' has three meaningful parts: un, kind and ly. Each of these parts is which of the following?

options.why: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.
Correct. A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that held the pen between the teeth
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group that held the pen between the lips
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Research shows that therapy works better when the client and therapist trust each other and agree on goals. What is this relationship called?

options.why: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
Correct. The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.explanation: The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.stem: Patients on a hospital ward earn points for making their beds and attending therapy, and trade the points for snacks and privileges. Which treatment is this?

options.why: Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.
Correct. A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.

questions.explanation: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters?

options.why: The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
Correct. The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.
A dendrite is a branching extension of a neuron that receives messages from other neurons.

questions.explanation: The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Consent is obtained before the study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal?

options.why: Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.
Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits?

options.why: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
A personality inventory is a questionnaire with many true-false or agree-disagree items that measures a range of traits.
Correct. Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.explanation: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.stem: A fifteen-year-old debates what would happen to society if people could live forever. Which of Piaget's stages allows this hypothetical thinking?

options.why: Correct. The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.stem: After a large, relaxed dinner, Ana's body directs energy toward digestion and her breathing slows. Which part of the nervous system is most active?

options.why: Correct. The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.
The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The somatic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles.

questions.explanation: The parasympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life?

options.why: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Correct. Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 11, 10, 8, 10, 7, 14, 24. What is the range of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
That is the mean.
Correct. Subtract the lowest score from the highest.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 7, 8, 10, 10, 11, 14, 24. Subtract the lowest score from the highest. The one very high score pulls the mean (12) above the median (10), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an external locus of control?

options.text: An explanation of behavior that points to the person's own traits or character
options.why: That describes a dispositional attribution.

options.text: The belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people
options.why: Correct. This is what an external locus of control means.

options.text: The comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse
options.why: That describes downward social comparison.

options.text: The comparing of oneself with people who are doing better
options.why: That describes upward social comparison.

questions.explanation: An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question?

options.why: State-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Correct. Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.
A retrieval cue is a stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind.

questions.explanation: Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.

questions.stem: Avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.explanation: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: Without considering any alternatives, Ravi plans to join the family business because his parents always expected it. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: Marc reads the assigned novel only because he wants a good grade. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: Correct. Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: A factory worker is paid for every twenty shirts she sews. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: Correct. A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing?

options.why: The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
Correct. The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.explanation: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.stem: Dee washes her hands forty times a day to relieve her worry. This repeated action is which of the following?

options.why: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.
Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).
Correct. A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.

questions.explanation: A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes closure?

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike
options.why: That describes similarity.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object
options.why: Correct. This is what closure means.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background
options.why: That describes figure and ground.

options.text: The Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other
options.why: That describes proximity.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Although Pat sincerely says she treats everyone equally, a reaction-time test shows she links one group with negative words more quickly. The test has revealed which of the following?

options.why: Correct. An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.

questions.explanation: An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 high school students. What does this most limit?

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: A depressed client believes she is worthless, that the world is unfair and that nothing will ever improve. This pattern is called which of the following?

options.why: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Correct. The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.explanation: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray?

options.why: Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors?

options.why: Correct. The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.

questions.explanation: The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the general adaptation syndrome?

options.text: The third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely
options.why: That describes the exhaustion phase.

options.text: The first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated
options.why: That describes the alarm reaction.

options.text: The second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor
options.why: That describes the resistance phase.

options.text: Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion
options.why: Correct. This is what the general adaptation syndrome means.

questions.explanation: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Mia's parents are loving but let her stay up as late as she likes and rarely enforce any rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Correct. Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.stem: After failing a quiz, Ty says, 'I am just not a math person,' and stops trying. Which belief does this show?

options.why: An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
A growth mindset is the belief that intelligence can be developed through effort and learning.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.
Correct. A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.

questions.explanation: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes procedural memory?

options.text: The memory to carry out a planned action in the future
options.why: That describes prospective memory.

options.text: The explicit memory of facts and general knowledge
options.why: That describes semantic memory.

options.text: The explicit memory of personally experienced events
options.why: That describes episodic memory.

options.text: The implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions
options.why: Correct. This is what procedural memory means.

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.stem: Walking to the phone, Rosa repeats a number again and again so that she does not forget it. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Correct. Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes general intelligence?

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

options.text: The theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal
options.why: That describes multiple intelligences.

options.text: The level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test
options.why: That describes mental age.

options.text: The single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks
options.why: Correct. This is what general intelligence means.

questions.explanation: General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with?

options.why: Correct. Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.
The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.

questions.explanation: Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a drug that blocks the reuptake of serotonin to treat a patient's depression. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
Correct. An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates?

options.why: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Correct. The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.
Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.

questions.explanation: The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control?

options.why: Correct. Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.

questions.explanation: Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources?

options.why: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Correct. The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.

questions.explanation: The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that waited with four other people
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which sense sends its signals to the brain without first passing through the thalamus?

options.why: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Correct. Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.explanation: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 84 office workers. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: After a railway accident damaged the front of his brain, Phineas Gage became impulsive and unable to plan. Which lobes were damaged?

options.why: The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
Correct. The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.

questions.explanation: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.stem: A stroke in the left motor cortex paralyzes a patient's right arm. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Correct. Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.explanation: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls?

options.why: Correct. A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.

questions.stem: The group given the nausea-causing injection drank less sweetened water. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The type of injection given after drinking and preference for sweetened water are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The type of injection given after drinking caused the difference in preference for sweetened water
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Although her son failed the exam, a mother makes clear that she values and accepts him just the same. In humanistic theory, this is which of the following?

options.why: A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
Correct. Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.explanation: Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking?

options.why: The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.
The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.
Correct. The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.explanation: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger?

options.why: Correct. Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.
Leptin is the hormone released by fat cells that signals fullness and reduces hunger.
Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.

questions.explanation: Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.

questions.stem: A small dot disappears when its image falls on the place where the optic nerve leaves the retina. What is this place called?

options.why: The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
Correct. The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.explanation: The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are between 480 and 520?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (480 and 520 are one standard deviation from the mean; 460 and 540 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the reporting of an emergency

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the reporting of an emergency.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The reporting of an emergency was defined as the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. On average, the value was 196 for the group that waited with four other people and 58 for the group that waited alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 80 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. (196 compared with 58).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the number of other people present affects the reporting of an emergency. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the number of other people present. The finding illustrates the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: people feel less personal duty to act when others are present.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
